observations.text: x subscript one through x subscript n
observations.title: Observations

summation.text: sum of x subscript i, for i from one to n
summation.title: Summation

mean.text: The arithmetic mean is the sum of all n observations divided by n.
mean.title: Arithmetic mean

mode.text: The mode is the value or values x at which the frequency f of x is largest.
mode.title: Mode

weighted-mean.text: Sum of weight times value, divided by the sum of weights
weighted-mean.title: Weighted mean

geometric-mean.text: The nth root of the product of the n positive observations
geometric-mean.title: Geometric mean

harmonic-mean.text: n divided by the sum of the reciprocals of the observations
harmonic-mean.title: Harmonic mean

balance.text: The sum of deviations from the sample mean is zero
balance.title: Balance

variance-example.text: For 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: population variance is 10 divided by 5, or 2; population standard deviation is the square root of 2, about 1.4142. Sample variance is 10 divided by 4, or 2.5; sample standard deviation is the square root of 2.5, about 1.5811.
variance-example.title: Variance and standard deviation

interpolation.text: x subscript k plus alpha times the difference between x subscript k plus one and x subscript k
interpolation.title: Interpolation

population-variance.text: Sum of squared deviations from the mean, divided by n
population-variance.title: Population variance

sample-variance.text: Sample variance s squared equals the sum of squared deviations from the sample mean divided by n minus one
sample-variance.title: Sample variance

moments.text: The kth central moment m subscript k is the average of the kth powers of deviations from the mean. Skewness g subscript one equals the third moment divided by the second moment to the power three halves. Excess kurtosis g subscript two equals the fourth moment divided by the square of the second moment, minus three.
moments.title: Standardized moments

corrected-moments.text: Corrected sample skewness G subscript one equals the square root of n times n minus one, divided by n minus two, times g subscript one. Corrected sample excess kurtosis G subscript two equals n minus one divided by the product of n minus two and n minus three, multiplied by the quantity n plus one times g subscript two plus six.
corrected-moments.title: Corrected sample shape measures

shape-domains.text: n at least three and n at least four
shape-domains.title: Shape domains

log-transform.text: log of x when lambda equals zero
log-transform.title: Log transform

covariance-example.text: For the paired example: population covariance equals 7 divided by 5, or 1.4. Sample covariance equals 7 divided by 4, or 1.75. Correlation r equals 7 divided by the square root of 10 times 18, approximately 0.5217.
covariance-example.title: Covariance and correlation

portfolio.text: Portfolio variance is weight one squared times variance one, plus weight two squared times variance two, plus twice weight one times weight two times the covariance of X and Y.
portfolio.title: Two-asset portfolio variance
